samples_judged.question_text: What number is marked on the number line?
Move the dot to show 263 on the number line.
Use base-10 blocks to show the number 203.
What number do the blocks show?
Move the dot to show 305 on the number line.
What number do the blocks show?

What number do the blocks show?

verdicts.reasoning: Recognition and representation both appear as separate task types: seeds 57 and 11 ask the pupil to name what the blocks or the number line already show, while seeds 42 and 23 hand over a numeral (203, 263) and require the pupil to build or place it.

The objects of every task are whole numbers — 751 on the number line at seed 11, 276 from the blocks at seed 78, 782 to be built at seed 91 — with content_type recorded as whole_number on the line items.

The sampled values reach the top end of the three-digit range without crossing it: 914 at seed 103, 816 at seed 127 and 782 at seed 91, with the smallest at 203 (seed 42), so the whole 'up to 1000' band is exercised.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: The thousands field is 0 in every PlaceValueBlocks payload and no sample reaches 1000 itself, so the boundary value named by the competency is never actually shown.

verdicts.reasoning: Base-10 blocks — the standard concrete manipulative — carry three of the samples: seed 42 has the pupil assemble 2 hundreds and 3 ones for 203 and seed 91 assemble 7/8/2 for 782 with is_interactive true, and seed 57 reads a value off a 5/5/4 block arrangement. It is a screen rendering of a concrete model rather than physical material, which is the closest a rendered item can come.

Two distinct pictorial models are drawn rather than one: a labelled NumberLine spanning 750-760 with a dot at 751 (seed 11) and 260-270 for the dot placement at seed 23, plus the block picture at seed 118 that must be read as 497.

Numerals are used as a representation the pupil must map to and from: seed 42 gives the numeral 203 in the stem as the thing to build, and seeds 57 and 127 require choosing the numeral (554, 816) that matches the block picture.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: The short distractors 14 (seed 57), 20 (seed 118) and 15 (seed 127) are the digit sums of the block counts — a sensible 'counted the pieces' misconception, but they sit oddly beside the three-digit options and may read as typos to a pupil.
